changeAssessments.assessment: No standalone fund CCP definition was found in the actual definitions and derivative provisions. The current fund rule retains the OTC 5/10% counterparty ceilings. The linked current regulation addresses netting, collateral and risk measurement without an express qualifying-CCP exclusion. UCITS Article 1(7) permits certain stricter domestic general requirements, but its no-conflict condition prevents treating that option as an automatic cure. No affected fund or denied transaction was identified.

The current 40% numerator still names derivatives, with a supervised-financial-counterparty exception; the combined20% rule also includes derivative exposures. The original new EU first subparagraph concerns securities and money-market instruments. Stricter-national-option, qualifying-clearing and actual exposure equivalence remain inconclusive.

Current internal rules expressly include CCP concentration and EMIR 7a conditions. Board responsibilities, proportionality and reports are operative routes; actual institution controls were not audited.

changes.ut-good-faith: L212-1 defines unfairness by significant imbalance without making proof of a separate good-faith breach a prerequisite. This can provide wider protection under EU Article 8; no gap inferred from omitted words.
changes.ut-conclusion: L212-1 expressly assesses circumstances existing at contract conclusion and all linked terms and contracts.
changes.ut-renewal: L215-1 provides dedicated advance notice before the objection period ends, free termination and refunds if notice omitted. L212-1 general unfairness also covers other terms and contracts; service-law sectoral exceptions do not themselves prove an unfairness exemption.
changes.ut-seller-definition: Current preliminary article, points 1–3: natural-person consumer outside profession; professional includes natural/legal, public/private persons, acting for another professional.
changes.ut-price-scope: L212-1 excludes main subject and adequacy of price or remuneration relative to the sold good/service only where clear and comprehensible. It does not exempt every price term.
changes.ut-mandatory-terms: No free-standing broad exemption for seller-created terms in current L212-1. EU Article 1(2) exception is not a duty to reduce stronger national protection. Specific mandatory sectoral rules not exhaustively certified.
changes.ut-binding-contract: L241-1: unfair terms deemed unwritten; rest of contract survives if capable; rule is mandatory public policy.
changes.ut-prevention: Current L621-7 and L621-8 permit collective injunctions and removal from proposed, intended and existing contracts, declaration unwritten in identical contracts and notice to consumers. L524-1–2 provide public-authority court routes; R632-1 requires ex officio exclusion after hearing parties.
changes.ut-sole-will: R212-2(1) expressly covers professional performance depending on its sole will; mandatory general L212-1 applies.
changes.ut-price-date: R212-1(3) prohibits unilateral price change in blacklisted scope, with defined R212-3–4 financial and indefinite-contract qualifications; general imbalance review remains. No requirement to copy each indicative Annex phrase.
changes.ut-insurance: The corrected recital is interpretive, not an independent new prohibition or requirement to exclude insurer liability. No broad insurance exemption established in L212-1; separate insurance procedures not certified.
changes.ut-interest-received: R212-4 first paragraph expressly covers interest owed by AND owed to the consumer, valid reason, prompt information and immediate termination. Whole R212-3–4 exceptions actually read.
changes.ut-terminology: L212-1 and R212-1–5 use clauses abusives with the operative imbalance test. Word differences alone not treated as a breach.
changes.ut-cz-reprint: Original definitions, negotiation scope, proof, transparency, survival, prevention and conflict law assessed against preliminary article, L212-1, L211-1, L241-1, L232-1, L621-7–8, L524-1–2 and R632-1. All 17 indicative Annex examples considered: a R212-1(6); b (5)–(7); c R212-2(1); d (2); e (3); f R212-1(7)–(9)/R212-2(4); g R212-2(4); h L215-1 plus L212-1; i R212-1(1); j (3)/R212-2(6); k R212-1(3); l same plus general imbalance; m (4); n (2); o (5); p R212-2(5); q R212-1(12)/R212-2(9)–(10). L212-1 covers negotiated and unnegotiated terms, and grey-list proof falls on the professional. L211-1 clarity and consumer-favourable interpretation exclude L621-8 collective proceedings.
changes.ut-notifications: Actual Article 8 a Commission notification performance not verified; no inference from silence in the domestic code.
changes.ut-penalties-general: L241-2 administrative sanctions concern irrebuttably blacklisted terms; L241-1-1 civil fine concerns continued use after final judgment. These are expressly permitted EU Article 8 b(2) options. General effectiveness in every outcome not certified.
changes.ut-penalty-factors: Current L522-1–10 administrative procedure actually read, including reasoned decision and cumulative sanctions. No express complete six-factor Article 8 b(3) route located in these bodies; wider constitutional/judicial and administrative guidance routes remain unclosed. Partial-review blocker, not proof of omission.
changes.ut-wide-penalties: L241-2 and L241-1-1 allow 4% of average of last three known annual turnovers and EUR2m when data unavailable, for CPC widespread infringements following a mutual-assistance request under L511-10. L511-10 includes requests by another Member State OR the Commission. Whether every required Article21 coordinated-action scenario is reached, and the turnover basis, require interpretation. No uncovered cohort established; HOLD public. Independent EU-side challenge: coordinated action by agreement need not use separate mutual assistance (CPC17(1),19(2),21); national equivalence remains open. EU text specifies no particular turnover reference year, so a three-year average is not treated as a demonstrated breach.
changes.ut-penalty-notification: L241-2 current note confirms 28 May2022 application; L241-1-1 later amended3May2025. Actual EU notification dates and performance unverified.

review.currentness: Actual Légifrance consolidated article and chapter bodies read with live header 26 October 2026. L241-1-1 and L621-7 incorporate the 3 May 2025 reform; L522-6 and L522-9-1 incorporate the 2 July 2025 reform.
review.assessmentScope: All 19 changed-meaning groups mapped. Formal legal-text comparison only; actual Commission notification, all sectoral procedures and enforcement outcomes not certified.
review.completionBlocker: The binding route for all six indicative Article 8 b(3) penalty criteria has not been closed. Interpretation of the mutual-assistance trigger for the Article 21 CPC maximum also remains open; no public allegation.
review.limitations: Partial review, with actual current primary bodies read. No deficient decision, harmed consumer or uncovered coordinated-action cohort identified. Annex examples are indicative and non-exhaustive; no demand for verbatim national copying.
review.legalConclusion: No defensible new public case established. Most corrected meanings are expressly present or receive wider national protection. Penalty trigger, turnover basis and indicative criteria remain qualified research questions.

review.independentReview: Reference agent independently read authentic CPC Regulation Articles17,19,21. Coordinated action may begin by agreement under17(1), with mutual assistance optional under19(2); Art21 imposes enforcement duties without universally requiring a separate request. This supports retaining the precise French request-trigger qualification, not a breach conclusion. National French bodies were read by root only. Reference withdrew a claimed preceding-financial-year rule: EU Art8b4 specifies annual turnover but no reference year; nonbinding Commission2021 parallel Omnibus guidance likewise says the year is undefined. No three-year-average breach inferred.
review.adverseReview: Root read official CCA2021 report sections41–46 and51: administrative punitive sanctions already subject to constitutional proportionality; indicative factors and coordinated actions discussed, with optional legislative precision proposed. This is earlier institutional discussion, not proof that the exact present request-trigger question has been recognised. Report predates current increased maxima and civil-fine reform; cannot support an ongoing omission from old monetary limits. General binding proportionality may supply part of the criteria route, but full six-factor reach remains unclosed. Root also read the entire official2021 ordinance report: Article8 explanation expressly describes the civil fine as following mutual assistance, but describes the administrative4%route more generally as cross-border cooperation. This supports an interpretation question rather than a categorical national gap; the report does not close the full binding six-factor route. Commission implementation-study section1.1.1.11 includes France among countries adopting the criteria to a greater or lesser degree; it does not identify a complete French binding route for each criterion. This is adverse context against claiming omission, while the source-level blocker remains.

changes.ut-good-faith: Article 82(1): terms contrary to good faith causing significant imbalance are unfair; mandatory classification.
changes.ut-conclusion: Article 82(3) expressly assesses circumstances at contract conclusion, not later performance.
changes.ut-renewal: Article 85(2) prohibits automatic fixed-term renewal where the deadline does not effectively allow objection; broader general unfairness remains in Article 82.
changes.ut-seller-definition: Articles 2–4 cover natural and legal traders, public and private, acting directly or through another person.
changes.ut-price-scope: Articles 80, 82–83 and 85 do not reproduce a blanket main-subject or price-adequacy exclusion; stronger review is permitted by Directive Article 8. Current court interpretation not certified.
changes.ut-mandatory-terms: Law 7/1998 Article 4 actually read: international convention terms and generally applicable mandatory statutory/administrative rules excluded; no broader seller-created exclusion established. Consumer-code Article 59 preserves sectoral minimum protection.
changes.ut-binding-contract: Article 83 makes unfair terms void and unwritten while preserving the contract if it can subsist; transparency nullity also applies.
changes.ut-prevention: Articles 53–54 permit injunctions against continued or imminently repeated conduct, including recommendations of unfair terms; public bodies, consumer organisations, prosecutor and eligible foreign bodies have standing.
changes.ut-sole-will: Article 85(7) expressly covers performance dependent solely on the trader’s will.
changes.ut-price-date: Article 85(10) compares final price to the price initially agreed, with objective-reason/termination and lawful index safeguards.
changes.ut-insurance: No separate exclusion of all insurance liability found in Articles 80–91. This corrected EU recital does not itself impose a new freestanding national prohibition.
changes.ut-interest-received: Article 85(3) expressly includes interest owed by the consumer OR to the consumer, lawful index or valid reason, prompt notice and immediate penalty-free termination.
changes.ut-terminology: Articles 82–91 use unfair-term terminology with the correct operative good-faith/imbalance test; no word-copy requirement inferred.
changes.ut-cz-reprint: Articles 3–4, 80, 82–83, 85–91, 53–54 and 67 read, including burden, transparency, all blacklist groups, survival, collective remedies and conflict-law protection. Law 7/1998 cross-reference remains to close. Law 7/1998 Articles 4, 8, 12, 16 and 19 now read; exclusion, nullity and collective injunction routes assessed.
changes.ut-notifications: Actual Commission notification performance is outside this formal national-law assessment; domestic higher protection considered, not treated as an automatic violation.
changes.ut-penalties-general: Articles 47(j), 48 and 49 sanction introduction/existence of unfair terms and failure to remove their effects; benefits, culpability, deterrence and proportionality addressed.
changes.ut-penalty-factors: Articles 48(3)–(5), 49(2)–(3) cover nature, culpability, duration, consumer harm, corrective action, recidivism, benefit, cross-border sanctions and economic capacity.
changes.ut-wide-penalties: Article 49(5) confines the CPC 4%/EUR 2 m maximum to very serious offences, while Article 48(2)(b) initially grades abusive-term offences as serious. Full adverse review considered mandatory upgrades, illicit-benefit multiples, regional-law floors and central CPC competence. No defensible uncovered cohort or binding interpretation established; legal result inconclusive, no public case.
changes.ut-penalty-notification: 2021 national reform applied 28 May 2022, as current article notes confirm. Actual Commission notification is not inferred from national text.

acts.title: Firearms
acts.inventoryStatus: Complete original 1991 provisions and annexes, 2008/51 and 2017/853 amending bodies, and 2021/555 operative Articles 1–28 plus Annexes I–IV read. All 12 direct corrigenda and 17 recursive corrigenda reviewed in authentic languages. Three 1991 R 01 legacy HTML tables recovered from official PDF/A 1 b editions: DE/IT B 5 AND→OR, EL can→cannot. No unresolved table-format blocker; the German national comparison is partial and the other country comparisons remain pending.

changeInventory.change: Expanded firearm and convertibility definitions; essential components include upper and lower receivers. Covers ammunition, dealers, brokers, illicit manufacturing, trafficking and tracing, including inherited translation corrections. Polish combustible-propellant and essential-component terms, Hungarian round-versus-magazine terms, Finnish alternatives and Romanian receiver terminology are included.
changeInventory.mandatory: Subject to express Member State options, stronger-protection permission and transitions.

changeInventory.change: Alternative official proof of residence; a non-transferable firearms pass valid for at most five years, with weapon, loss and other updates. The ten-year category D exception in the original 1991 text was removed by 2008/51 Article 1(1)(e), then retained as removed in 2017 and 2021. Includes the Hungarian correction requiring lawful acquisition AND holding.
changeInventory.mandatory: Subject to express Member State options, stronger-protection permission and transitions.

changeInventory.change: Remove the blanket collector and museum exclusion; retain specified armed-forces, police, public-authority and defence-transfer exclusions. Stricter national protection remains subject to traveller rights. Rights attach to residence, not nationality.
changeInventory.mandatory: Subject to express Member State options, stronger-protection permission and transitions.

changeInventory.change: Clear unique marking and registration for firearms manufactured or imported on or after 14 September 2018 and placed on the market; essential-component marking, historical and small-component options, ammunition-package marks and a government-to-civilian transfer mark.
changeInventory.mandatory: Subject to express Member State options, stronger-protection permission and transitions.

changeInventory.change: Registration, licensing or authorisation, and integrity and ability checks for both dealers and brokers. For a legal person, checks cover the entity and the natural persons directing it.
changeInventory.mandatory: Subject to express Member State options, stronger-protection permission and transitions.

changeInventory.change: Computerised records identify each firearm and its essential components, conversions and ownership. Retention extends 30 years after destruction, with ten-year licensing/customs access and thirty-year criminal-law access, plus purpose-based deletion rules. Earlier 2008 requirements and their 31 December 2014 deadline are followed.
changeInventory.mandatory: Subject to express Member State options, stronger-protection permission and transitions.

changeInventory.change: Dealers and brokers record all firearms received or disposed of and hand records over on closure. Electronic reporting must occur without undue delay, with immediate authority updates and continuous ownership links. Includes the Finnish 2008 correction on all firearms and receiver data.
changeInventory.mandatory: Subject to express Member State options, stronger-protection permission and transitions.

changeInventory.change: Licence or specific national permission for category C, good cause, age eighteen and no-danger conditions. Supervised youth hunting and target-shooting exceptions concern acquisition other than purchase. Includes Lithuanian and Hungarian corrections on those distinctions.
changeInventory.mandatory: Subject to express Member State options, stronger-protection permission and transitions.

changeInventory.change: Monitor continuing authorisation conditions, including relevant medical and psychological information; withdraw permissions when conditions cease. Large centre-fire magazines can require category B withdrawal unless an applicable authorisation or grandfathering route exists. Do not prohibit an otherwise lawful firearm merely because it was acquired abroad.
changeInventory.mandatory: Subject to express Member State options, stronger-protection permission and transitions.

changeInventory.change: Secure storage, supervision and transport must prevent unauthorised access. Firearms and ammunition must not be readily accessible together; scrutiny is proportionate to quantity and category.
changeInventory.mandatory: Subject to express Member State options, stronger-protection permission and transitions.

changeInventory.change: For distance purchases, an authorised dealer, broker or authority verifies identity and required authorisation before or on delivery. Applies to category A–C firearms, essential components and ammunition. Includes the Slovenian correction and updated consumer distance-contract definition.
changeInventory.mandatory: Subject to express Member State options, stronger-protection permission and transitions.

changeInventory.change: Prohibit acquisition and holding of category A firearms, essential components and ammunition; impound unlawful items.
changeInventory.mandatory: Subject to express Member State options, stronger-protection permission and transitions.

changeInventory.change: Optional, individually reasoned security, defence, educational, research and historical exemptions. Collector registers, monitoring and strict security also matter; dealer, broker and museum routes have safeguards. Member States need not adopt every optional relaxation.
changeInventory.mandatory: Subject to express Member State options, stronger-protection permission and transitions.

changeInventory.change: An optional category A6/7 target-shooting authorisation requires medical checks, active competition, twelve months of club training and a qualifying discipline. Includes the limited conscription-related option and review at most every five years.
changeInventory.mandatory: Subject to express Member State options, stronger-protection permission and transitions.

changeInventory.change: Optional multi-year acquisition permissions require notification and continuing-condition checks. Possession authorisations are reviewed at most every five years and renewed only while conditions remain satisfied.
changeInventory.mandatory: Subject to express Member State options, stronger-protection permission and transitions.

changeInventory.change: Optional grandfathering for formerly category B weapons acquired and registered before 13 June 2017. C234/21 interprets overlapping A9 conversions; it does not annul the directive. Existing 2008 category B holders need no fresh application for their lawfully held C/D weapons, while later transferees must obtain or hold permission.
changeInventory.mandatory: Subject to express Member State options, stronger-protection permission and transitions.

changeInventory.change: Category C declaration and transfer notifications include a non-resident’s home Member State. The optional delay for older C5–7 firearms expired on 14 March 2021. Includes the Hungarian reversed-date correction and the 1991 correction covering all relevant C firearms.
changeInventory.mandatory: Subject to express Member State options, stronger-protection permission and transitions.

changeInventory.change: Ammunition possession follows equivalent firearm conditions. Large centre-fire magazines require the specified authorisation. Dealers and brokers may refuse suspicious transactions and must report attempts. Includes the Hungarian complete-round correction.
changeInventory.mandatory: Subject to express Member State options, stronger-protection permission and transitions.

changeInventory.change: Alarm and signal weapons must be non-convertible; convertible devices count as firearms. Includes the Czech cartridge-chamber correction and chemical-energy scope. Technical standards apply to the specified post-14 September 2018 cohort.
changeInventory.mandatory: Subject to express Member State options, stronger-protection permission and transitions.

changeInventory.change: Essential components must be irreversibly disabled, with authority verification, certificate AND mark. Legacy possession is distinguished from placing on the market or transferring. Earlier national standards require the relevant EU equivalence determination, notification and technical fallback.
changeInventory.mandatory: Subject to express Member State options, stronger-protection permission and transitions.

changeInventory.change: Distance transfers follow the same procedure. A dealer general authorisation lasts at most three years. The departure Member State receives advance information and may inspect. The exemption list identifies goods that may enter WITHOUT prior consent; English and Swedish corrections do not reverse that meaning.
changeInventory.mandatory: Subject to express Member State options, stronger-protection permission and transitions.

changeInventory.change: EFP travel routes cover hunters and historical re-enactors with C firearms and target shooters with B/C and qualifying A firearms, subject to activity evidence and the specified restrictions. Acceptance cannot carry a fee. Includes Swedish and Danish corrections distinguishing target shooting from competition alone.
changeInventory.mandatory: Subject to express Member State options, stronger-protection permission and transitions.

changeInventory.change: Electronic exchange covers transfer authorisations and refusals for security OR reliability. Includes German and Hungarian corrections, national contact details, regular cooperation and destination/transit notifications.
changeInventory.mandatory: Subject to express Member State options, stronger-protection permission and transitions.

changeInventory.change: Effective, proportionate and dissuasive penalties and enforcement arrangements are required; a standard of mere sufficiency is not equivalent.
changeInventory.mandatory: Subject to express Member State options, stronger-protection permission and transitions.

changeInventory.change: Category A includes converted automatic firearms, specified loaded high-capacity centre-fire firearms, functional folding long firearms and acoustic conversions. Includes missile AND launcher, armour-piercing terms, and the lawful hunting OR target-shooting expanding-ammunition exception.
changeInventory.mandatory: Subject to express Member State options, stronger-protection permission and transitions.

changeInventory.change: Revised category B capacity, smooth-bore, repeating and semi-automatic distinctions. Capacity is more than three rounds, not at least three. For the at-most-three-round B 5 rule, detachable loading device OR uncertainty that ordinary tools cannot increase capacity: German and Italian 1991 R 01 correct AND to OR; Greek corrects can contain to cannot contain. Historical definitions are followed through 2017 and 2021.
changeInventory.mandatory: Subject to express Member State options, stronger-protection permission and transitions.

changeInventory.change: C5 acoustic conversions, C6 deactivated firearms and C7 single-shot smooth-bore long firearms are included; category D is deleted. Modern reproductions are not exempt merely because they look antique.
changeInventory.mandatory: Subject to express Member State options, stronger-protection permission and transitions.

changeInventory.euLocator: 2021/555 Annex I-III/IV; 1991 R 04 DEU/FIN, R 08 FIN, R 11 POL
changeInventory.change: Short firearm means barrel at most thirty centimetres OR overall length at most sixty. Semi-automatic means one shot per trigger operation; repeating includes magazine OR cylinder; automatic means multiple shots per operation. changes.fw-definitions: WaffG Section 1 and Annex 1 include convertible firearms, essential upper/lower receivers, split bolts, ammunition and commercial mediation. Definitions and broader domestic licensing were personally read. Exact treatment of every technical term remains qualified by statutory classification and scope.
changes.fw-residence-pass: Current AWaffV Section 33(1) retains an initial ten-year term for the narrow hunter/sports-shooter single-shot smooth-bore cohort. The original 1991 category D exception was removed by 2008/51 Article 1(1)(e), due 28 July 2010. Some official guidance still gives ten years; other guidance describes five. Published as a qualified document-validity lead after independent adverse review, with no actual issued pass or travel outcome established. Alternative residence proof and full current pass template still require closure.
changes.fw-scope: WaffG Sections 17–18 license collectors and experts; Section 55 retains specified public-service exemptions. The separate current KrWaffKontrG Sections 1–7, 10–13 and 15 were read, including manufacture/transfer permits, entity and director reliability, supervision, records, seizure and state-service exclusions. Full technical classification and all separate-regime transitions remain unclosed.
changes.fw-marks: WaffG Section 24 and AWaffV Section 21 require marking of firearms and essential components, including government-to-civilian transfers, with small-part and historical exceptions. Whole Section 21 was read; the linked technical standards and commencement instruments require final mapping.
changes.fw-dealers-brokers: WaffG Sections 21 and 21a license manufacturing/trade and managers, while Annex 1 Section 2 No 9 includes commercial mediation. Actual official WaffVwV Sections 21.1–21.10 and 21a were read: entity permissions, partner/directing-person reliability checks, register inquiries, foreign applicants and manager permissions. The instruction is from 2012 and does not certify every later administrative practice; no uncovered entity or manager established.
changes.fw-database: Whole current WaffRG Sections 1–34 read, including linked weapon, component, owner and permission data; conversions; updates; access; purpose limits and deletion. Section 27 says deletion at the latest 30 years after destruction, while WaffG Section 44a requires at least 30-year tracing records. Exact combined retention equivalence is legally inconclusive; no early deletion was established.
changes.fw-transaction-registers: WaffG Sections 37–37f require electronic immediate dealer reports and detailed weapon/component data; WaffRG Sections 8–9 route them to the register. Short repair and stock-transfer exceptions use substitute documentation, with AWaffV Sections 17–20 retention/handover. Timeliness and continuous ownership equivalence remain qualified; no untraced weapon established.
changes.fw-licence-age: WaffG Sections 2–4, 10, 12–14 and 27 license ordinary firearms and regulate minimum age, need, suitability and supervised youth hunting/sport. Section 27 was read in full. Exceptions concern limited supervised use; no general underage-purchase exception established.
changes.fw-monitor-withdraw: WaffG Sections 4–6a require periodic reliability/suitability and need checks, medical/psychological evidence and adverse-information reporting; Sections 45–46 require withdrawal and surrender where conditions cease. The discretionary need exception and grandfathered magazines remain expressly qualified.
changes.fw-storage: WaffG Section 36 plus whole AWaffV Section 13 regulate unloaded secure storage, separate or protected ammunition, quantity-sensitive safes and temporary storage. Existing containers, collectors, shared households and individual alternative protection are qualified; actual access and inspections were not audited.
changes.fw-distance: WaffG Sections 34–35 require entitlement and identity checks and expressly address shipping, with transfer permissions under Sections 29–30 preserved. Essential components follow the Annex 1 treatment. No actual remote transaction was examined.
changes.fw-a-prohibition: WaffG Section 2(3), Annex 2 Section 1 and Sections 40–41 prohibit listed weapons and allow seizure. Broader domestic licensing also applies. Separate military-weapons regime and some A-category exceptions remain to close.
changes.fw-a-options: WaffG Sections 17–18 and 40 provide collector/expert and reasoned BKA exception routes with conditions. EU optional derogations do not require a national relaxation. Equivalence of any granted individual permission was not assessed.
changes.fw-a-target: WaffG Section 14 contains age, active club membership and discipline conditions; Section 40 and Annex 2 preserve prohibition and exceptions. Whether an optional A6/7 individual route is used and satisfies every EU condition requires companion-rule confirmation.
changes.fw-periodic: WaffG Section 4(3) requires reliability/suitability review at most every three years and Section 4(4) checks continuing need every five years. Section 10 indefinite possession documents therefore do not alone establish missing review.
changes.fw-grandfather: Whole WaffG Section 58 read, including 2020 provisions for components, converted firearms and magazines, pre-2017 positions and notification periods. A later transferee generally requires permission. Individual inherited permissions and all historical administrative decisions remain outside this formal-text assessment.
changes.fw-c-declarations: WaffG Sections 10 and 37a–37g, Annex 2 and AWaffV Sections 25a–25c cover ordinary licensed C weapons, converted/deactivated weapons, notifications and legacy transitions. Wider national licensing is not treated as an omission of EU declaration.
changes.fw-magazines-ammo: WaffG Sections 10 and 40, Annex 2 prohibitions and Section 58 grandfathering address ammunition and large magazines; Section 35(2) requires suspicious-transaction notification. Exact authorisation exceptions are qualified; no actual magazine acquisition examined.
changes.fw-alarm: Annex 1 convertibility definitions and Annex 2 exemptions refer to non-convertible alarm/signal weapons and notified Member State technical rules implementing Directive 2019/69. The older-model and technical conformity routes need final companion-source mapping.
changes.fw-deactivation: WaffG Section 39c and whole AWaffV Sections 25a–25c require certificates/marks and regulate legacy deactivation. Old domestic possession treatment does not carry across a Member State transfer. Verification authority and directly applicable technical regime remain to finish.
changes.fw-transfer: WaffG Sections 29–30 and whole AWaffV Sections 28–32 require destination permission or lawful exemption, advance departure reporting, supporting documents and a dealer general permission of at most three years. No identified reversal of the historical may-enter-without-consent correction.
changes.fw-travel: WaffG Sections 32 and 38 provide EFP plus activity-evidence routes for hunters, target shooters and re-enactors, with categories and firearm-number limits. General stronger protection does not automatically excuse interference with EU traveller rights; exact scope and fees remain to close.
changes.fw-information-exchange: AWaffV Section 32 expressly requires electronic, prompt transfer information and uses Regulation 2019/686; WaffRG Section 5 separately records refusals for security/reliability or personal aptitude. Exact refusal-exchange implementing route remains to read; no inference that all discretionary refusals must be exchanged.
changes.fw-penalties: WaffG Sections 51–54 were read, covering criminal sanctions, negligence, administrative offences, reporting/marking/storage contraventions and confiscation. Effective sanctions exist formally; proportionality and actual enforcement outcomes are not certified.
changes.fw-category-a: Whole WaffG Annexes 1–2 read. The A6–9 categories and military weapons references are present; expanding-ammunition definition uses hunting OR sport. Separate war-weapons scope and the relationship between category A8 and national prohibition remain qualified.
changes.fw-category-b: Annex 1 Section 3 No 2.6 literally omits the EU negation before the A7b reference. However, the official NWR XWaffe matrix assigns ordinary detachable-magazine semi-automatic long firearms to B2.6, while broad domestic licensing applies. Private HOLD only: no actual misclassification or home-state consent failure established; conforming interpretation is a substantial contrary route.
changes.fw-category-c: Annex 1 Section 3 Nos 3.5–3.7 includes converted acoustic, deactivated and single-shot smooth-bore weapons; Annex 2 and AWaffV Section 25c provide licensing/declaration and legacy rules. Modern antique-looking reproductions are not generally excluded merely by appearance.
changes.fw-technical-definitions: Annex 1 defines long firearms by both length conditions, so the short-weapon complement is an OR. Semi-automatic operation uses one shot per trigger operation. Repeat-fire wording and revolver classifications were read together; no cylinder exemption established.
changes.fw-pass-content: WaffG Sections 32, 37g and 38 plus AWaffV transfer particulars were read. Current pass template, complete Annex II warnings and category fields still need direct source review.
changes.fw-transitions: Current WaffG Section 58, AWaffV legacy rules and WaffRG Section 34 were read. National currentness does not prove historic timely transposition or actual Commission communication. Technical amender commencement and companion legal history remain open.

changes.1151-C2: Schedule 2 retains the optional low-strength beer band through 2.8%ABV. The EU permits, rather than requires, extending that band to 3.5%.

changes.1151-C4: No producer-specific small-wine rate is exercised in current Schedule 2. The optional new reduction is not mandatory; outbound certification is assessed separately.
changes.1151-C5: Current78D provides OFB relief with statutory partial-licensing and batch conditions. The actual mandatory APT5 note2 may instead channel every licensed producer into the small-cooperation declaration. This material administrative-condition alternative prevents a supported current omission; exact legal equivalence remains qualified.
changes.1151-C6: General excise sections 96,97,109 B and 109 O assess common alcohol movement and small-wine exceptions. The 2020 Article 15 change updates the framework citation; equal treatment of wine references for OFBs was already present. No new 2020 product-scope omission inferred. Optional specified-wine intermediate reduction not separately exercised.

Actual Revenue manual sections 1.9 and 5.9–5.11 recognise foreign certification or self-certification and current e-AD/e-SAD references. Actual requests, acceptance decisions and administrative practice are outside this assessment.
changes.1151-C11: Not applicable to national legislation: Commission implementing power.
changes.1151-C12: Current 77(c),(d) expressly cover foreign denaturing and manufacturing-equipment cleaning/maintenance. SI 379/2004 regulations 32–38 retain approval/use formalities; general 109 O provides completely-denatured movement treatment. Higher statutory right and consistent interpretation are material alternatives to an outdated-formality allegation; no actual refusal established.
changes.1151-C13: Current 73 medicinal-product definition references 2001/82 and 2001/83, including amending/replacing directives; section 77 manufacture exemption assessed.
changes.1151-C14: Optional 150 ml food-supplement exemption is not separately exercised; existing medicine/food exemptions assessed without treating the option as mandatory.
changes.1151-C15: Actual national denaturant approval, notified foreign complete-denaturing and control provisions read. Individual notifications, anti-abuse refusals and Commission performance are outside current-law assessment.
changes.1151-C17: Commission powers and conditional Member-State information duties do not independently require a national substantive rule. Actual reporting performance not audited.
changes.1151-C18: Current target provisions and authentic material commencement orders assessed. Historical EU-reference/publication and communication performance is not certified. Simplified amendment-table dates were not used where authentic commencement orders differed.

provisionChecks.evidence: S.I. 632/2025 Regulation 7 replaces principal Regulation 3(2): express application of more favourable general Act, chemical-agent and CMR safeguards. Current S.I. 122/2024 as amended by 128/2026 was independently read.
S.I. 632 Regulation 23 replaces Schedule 1 with six fibrous silicates classified as CLP category 1 A. Current asbestos Code Schedule 1 repeats the correct CAS numbers and types.

S.I. 632 Regulation 9(1) expressly prioritises removal in risk assessment. S.I. 589/2010 Regulation 3(d), replacing principal Regulation 15, requires a written plan and removal before other demolition except where that increases exposure risk.

S.I. 632 Regulation 9(2) limits principal Regulation 5(b) to disapplication of Regulation 11, removing old health/register exemptions. Regulation 11 now also contains the permit, creating the separately documented qualified scope concern.

S.I. 632 Regulation 13 requires training certificates, notification, work plan, risk assessment and prior permit number. Regulation 25 and Schedule 3 include worker lists, certificates, latest health assessment, site particulars, methods, decontamination, waste, air exchange and equipment.

S.I. 632 Regulation 11 requires technically lowest exposure, dust suppression, source suction, sedimentation, decontamination, confinement, cleaning and sealed transport/waste. Principal Schedule 2 hygiene now applies without the old exception.

S.I. 632 Regulation 12 requires operational-phase, personal representative samples and competent sampling/analysis. Principal Regulation 10(1) is triggered by an initial assessment at or above the limit, whereas current Code page 6 describes risk-based sampling. Equivalent effect for lower assessed levels remains legally inconclusive; no separate public outcome claim.

S.I. 632 Regulation 12 specifies electron microscopy or an equally/more accurate alternative now; current Code page 7 still recognises competent WHO 1997 phase-contrast microscopy. The EU electron/thin-fibre duty is not due until 21 December 2029. No current missed future deadline is inferred; the combined route remains an interpretation question.

Binding principal Regulation 6, replaced by S.I. 632 Regulation 10, incorporates the latest Code. The complete eight-page Code Schedule 1 sets the current 0.01 fibres/cm³ eight-hour TWA from 21 December 2025.

Actual Code Schedule 1 provides future 0.01 fibres/cm³ including fibres thinner than 0.2 µm and the 0.002 alternative from 21 December 2029. Future national choice and administration are not certified or treated as a current omission.

S.I. 632 Regulation 15 replaces principal Regulation 13(1): immediate stopping on exceedance or disturbance of previously unidentified asbestos, followed by cause identification and remedy. Retained Regulation 13(2) bars resumption until adequate protection.
S.I. 632 Regulation 15(2) limits respirator use and requires regular breaks appropriate to physical/climatic conditions, with consultation.

S.I. 632 Regulation 14 replaces principal Regulation 12(1): for pre-31 December 2004 premises, obtain owner/employer/register information or a competent survey before work; share survey information with another employer on request.
S.I. 632 Regulation 16 requires individually adjusted, fit-tested PPE and a sealed enclosure under mechanical extraction. Current Code page 6 also requires fit testing.

S.I. 632 Regulation 17 replaces principal Regulation 15(10), requiring written site clearance before other activities. The full Regulation 15 in S.I. 589/2010 retains competent independent analysis as appropriate.

S.I. 632 Regulations 19/28 and entire Schedule 7 cover initial, regular and needs-based theory/practice; competent trainers; five certificate fields; all subjects; profession-specific adaptation; and additional demolition/removal equipment training.

Principal Regulation 11(1)(a)(iv)/(b), inserted by S.I. 632 Regulation 13, requires a prior permit number and public list, but is expressly subject to Regulation 5(b). The whole of Regulation 11 is disapplied for qualifying intact low-risk removal. HSA issues a permit per notification. See qualified private candidate ie-asbestos-low-risk-permit-exception; no actual unpermitted work or harm shown.

S.I. 632 Regulation 21 replaces principal Regulation 24 with all medically diagnosed asbestos occupational diseases and doctor reporting. Regulation 27 adds lung/larynx/ovarian cancers and non-malignant pleural disease; Regulation 22 removes the low-risk register exemption. Actual principal Regulations 20–25 health and 40-year record routes were read.
Commission reviews require no separate national rule.

S.I. 632 was signed 17 December 2025 and states commencement on 21 December; notice was published 30 December. Current Code also commenced 21 December. Official histories updated 13 October 2026 list only the 2010 and 2025 amenders and show 632 unaffected. Historical Commission notification/performance was not audited.
Institutional delegation and reprinted existing recommendations create no independent new national duty.

changes.1151-C1: Beer is taxed by alcoholic strength under section 75 and Schedule 2, not degrees Plato. The revised Plato method and temporary continuation are not applicable to the Irish tax base.
changes.1151-C2: Schedule 2 retains the optional low-strength beer band through 2.8%ABV. The EU permits, rather than requires, extending that band to 3.5%.
changes.1151-C3: Actual 2021 section 43 deletes the frozen CNCode definition. Current 73(3) imports undefined Directive meanings, and its Directive definition expressly includes 2020/1151. Functional incorporation of the updated nomenclature assessed; no excluded classification established.
changes.1151-C4: No producer-specific small-wine rate is exercised in current Schedule 2. The optional new reduction is not mandatory; outbound certification is assessed separately.
changes.1151-C5: Current78D provides OFB relief with statutory partial-licensing and batch conditions. The actual mandatory APT5 note2 may instead channel every licensed producer into the small-cooperation declaration. This material administrative-condition alternative prevents a supported current omission; exact legal equivalence remains qualified.
changes.1151-C6: General excise sections 96,97,109 B and 109 O assess common alcohol movement and small-wine exceptions. The 2020 Article 15 change updates the framework citation; equal treatment of wine references for OFBs was already present. No new 2020 product-scope omission inferred. Optional specified-wine intermediate reduction not separately exercised.
changes.1151-C7: No small-producer intermediate-product reduction is exercised in current Schedule 2. The new option is not mandatory.

Actual requests, acceptance decisions and administrative practice are outside this assessment.

SI 379/2004 regulations 32–38 retain approval/use formalities; general 109 O provides completely-denatured movement treatment. changeAssessments.assessment: KAGB 28(1) no5 explicitly aligns data processing and network/information systems with DORA. Registered-manager scope and DORA exemptions remain relevant; no omitted update identified.
The altered Commission delegated mandate does not itself require a national duplicate mandate.

VAG 23(1),(4) requires legal compliance and continuity arrangements. DORA directly imposes applicable ICT continuity; VAG 35(2) no10 requires audit of DORA compliance, 295 designates authority and 308d supplies enforcement. No missing ICT protection inferred from the unchanged general wording.
The change narrows an EU delegated mandate; not a standalone national drafting requirement.
KAGB 28(1) no5 expressly references DORA systems for investment managers; scope/exempt registered managers must follow the underlying DORA perimeter.

KWG 44(1) extends information, copies and inspection powers to outsourcing undertakings, organs and employees. ICT providers within this broad outsourcing category are covered; no categorical omission identified.

KWG 25a(1) mandates legal compliance, technical organisation and IT emergency management; DORA applies directly, 6(1g) designates supervision and 2(2)/(2a) extends or simplifies its application for specified institutions.
KWG 25a(1) no5 plus directly applicable DORA Article 11 provides the ICT continuity route; no absent plan obligation inferred from generic statutory language.

KWG 6b(1)–(3) and 6(1g) cover operational-risk review and DORA supervision. ECB 2025 SREP section 5.5.1 expressly describes its adjusted DORA methodology and threat-led testing. Exact equivalence for all resilience-test results, particularly in BaFin LSI methodology, remains unverified; this formal-law assessment does not certify administrative implementation.
SAG 40 expressly includes digital operational resilience and DORA network/information systems in resolution-plan content.

SAG13(2), MaSanV3/6/15/25 and binding2016/1075 Articles 5/12 provide recovery-governance and continuous-IT-service analysis, alongside direct DORA 11. Simplified-plan exceptions and the precise alignment of recovery-plan content with DORA remain interpretive; no absence inferred from generic wording.

SAG42 expressly permits all necessary planning information and follows BRRD11(3) technical standards. Current binding2025/2303 Articles 2–6 and Annex I Z08.01 include critical-ICT-provider and DORA-service fields. Exact test-result information can be requested under the broad power, but no complete automatic template equivalent was established; actual authority requests were not audited.
SAG 57(3) expressly requires at least the matters in BRRD AnnexC; that cross-reference reaches the changed ICT agreements/incidents/testing criteria. 57(6) applies the information powers in42.
WpHG 80(1) nos1,4 expressly links continuity and information-system security to DORA.
WpHG 80(2) expressly aligns algorithmic-trading systems, continuity plans and testing with DORA ChaptersII/IV and Article 11.
BörsG 5(3) no2 expressly includes ICT risks under DORA ChapterII; generic technical-function controls coexist without establishing a contradictory duplicate.
BörsG 5(4a) requires DORA-compliant operational resilience and Article 11 continuity/recovery; 26d refers to ChaptersII/IV for arrangements and testing.
ZAG 2(1) no9 uses ICT-network terminology and retains the payment-initiation/account-information carve-outs from the technical-service exclusion.
ZAG 10(2) nos5,6,8 expressly requires DORA ICT arrangements, incident reporting and continuity/recovery plans in applications.
ZAG 26(1) expressly includes ICT systems, preserves management responsibility and supervisory access/control over outsourced activities.
ZAG 53(1) expressly preserves DORA ChapterII for the listed payment-service-provider categories.
ZAG 54(7) exempts the listed providers from 54(1)-(4) incident reporting; fraud-statistics reporting in54(5) remains distinct.
The altered EBA technical-standard mandate is an EU institutional task, not a domestic replication duty.

VAG23(4),234/234a supply pension-fund continuity governance; direct DORA ICT obligations and35/295/308d supervision apply within their own scope. No-more-than15-member IORP exclusion retained; no blanket duty inferred.
The 2025 correction concerns Hungarian only; no German drafting change is required for that terminology correction.
